sources.entry: Fmusic - A fmusic is a open source music player on SwiftUI.[![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/wandercn/fmusic)

summary.one_liner: fmusic is a local music player for macOS written in SwiftUI, with album metadata/cover parsing, lyrics download and karaoke-style display, and metadata editing.
summary.what_it_does: The README (written in Chinese) describes a local music player built with SwiftUI. It automatically parses album info and cover art from audio files, and plays flac, mp3, wav, m4a, aif and m4r files. Playback modes include sequential, loop, shuffle and repeat-one, with a draggable progress bar and volume control. The library can be imported from a folder via toolbar icon, menu or Cmd+O, and it supports fuzzy search over song, artist and album, a simple favorites feature, and a hideable sidebar. The song list offers a right-click menu to edit metadata (title, album, artist, track number), view file details and path, and rename files; it also downloads lyrics automatically (stored in ~/Music/Lyrics) and shows karaoke-style lyric highlighting when timestamp tags exist. A playlist feature is listed as not yet implemented.
use_cases: play local music library on mac
browse music by album and artist
search music library by title or artist
how_to_run: Clone the repository and open the project in Xcode (README mentions Xcode Version 13.4.1)
Build and run on macOS 11.0 or later
Alternatively, download the signed and notarized dmg from the latest release (v1.1.0 per README)
If macOS blocks the app as damaged, run: sudo xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/xxxx.app (replace with your app path)
notable: Automatic lyric download with karaoke-style highlighting for lyrics that have timestamp tags
Edits title, album, artist and track number tags written into the audio files (best compatibility with flac, mp3, m4a)
Signed and notarized dmg release, so no local build is needed
Fuzzy search across song name, artist and album
caveats: Playlist feature not implemented yet according to the README
Mac 10.15 compatibility is not confirmed; the author reports it fails to run on an Intel 10.15 machine and suggests a separate repo for that
